reconcile.connective: Commentators distinguish 1 Corinthians 7:14's 'sanctified' — a marital, not salvific, status — from actual salvation, and read Acts 16:31's household promise as conditioned on the household's own belief.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the tension by design, pairing 'saved through the believer' against 1 Corinthians 7:16's flat 'who knows?' as incompatible answers.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "If a husband believes, is his wife saved also?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/husband.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (online; contra/husband.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: This cannot be understood of internal sanctification, which is never the case; an unbeliever cannot be sanctified by a believer in this sense, for such a sanctification is only by the Spirit of God …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly denies that the 'sanctified' of 7:14 is the Spirit's saving sanctification, the specific distinction needed to reconcile it with 7:16's doubt about actually saving the spouse.

excerpts.excerpt_text: sanctified—Those inseparably connected with the people of God are hallowed thereby, so that the latter may retain the connection without impairing their own sanctity (compare Ti1 4:5); nay, rather imparting to the former externally some degree of their own hallowed character, and so preparing the way for the unbeliever becoming at last sanctified inwardly by faith.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Frames the external 'sanctified' status of 7:14 as preparatory to, not identical with, the unbeliever's eventual inward salvation by faith — directly addressing the 7:14/7:16 tension.

excerpts.excerpt_text: and thy house; or family, provided they believe in Christ also, as they did, Act 16:34 or otherwise there can be no salvation, for he that believeth not shall be damned.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Makes the jailer's household's salvation explicitly conditional on the household members' own belief — the same uncertainty 1 Corinthians 7:16 voices — resolving the Acts 16:31 vs. 7:16 half of the question.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on 1 Corinthians 7:14 and 7:16
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Haley's Alleged Discrepancies does not treat this specific pairing (checked; no coverage of 1 Cor 7:14/16 or Acts 16:31 in the 1874/1876 editions). Gill's exposition treats both 1 Corinthians 7:14 and 7:16, and Acts 16:31, at length and directly resolves the tension this row raises.

link.title: GotQuestions: What does the Bible say about household salvation?
link.note: Explicitly connects Acts 16:31 and 1 Corinthians 7:16, arguing the jailer's household verse is not a blanket automatic-salvation promise.
